intro.author: Traditionally Moses, who is said to write down some of its events and laws (17:14; 24:4; 34:27). Many scholars think the book was compiled from several sources over time.
intro.written: Traditionally during the wilderness years. The date of the Exodus itself is debated: many place it in the 1400s BC (based on 1 Kings 6:1), others in the 1200s BC.
intro.audience: The people of Israel, learning how God freed them and made them his own nation
intro.setting: Jacob's descendants have grown into a large people in Egypt, where a new Pharaoh forces them into slavery. The book moves from the brickfields of Egypt, through the sea, to Mount Sinai in the wilderness, where Israel camps for most of the story.
intro.purpose: To show how the LORD rescued Israel from slavery, bound them to himself in covenant at Sinai, and came to live among them in the tabernacle.
intro.bigIdea: The God who sets his people free comes to dwell among them.
